subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as a public per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 remain the landing path?
rationale: The source-reproduced gap is real, but adding these per-agent config blocks changes a public config contract and provider/session routing semantics, which requires maintainer product direction before automation should create another fix.

options.title: Sponsor the additive contract
options.body: Approve the broad per-agent config direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR or a replacement as the landing path.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` now and defer broader compaction/contextPruning knobs to a later design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline the config expansion and close or redirect implementation attempts, leaving users with global defaults or separate instances.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the additive contract
recommendation.body: Approve the broad per-agent config direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR or a replacement as the landing path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across compaction runtime, config docs, and adjacent product/config decisions for this surface.
